ref.substituent_description: A piperidine ring: the carbon at position 4 (opposite the N) bears EtO by a solid wedge, and the carbon next to N (position 2) bears a benzene ring by a hashed bond; the piperidine N is bonded to a CH2 attached to C4 of an indole. On the indole: MeO on C5 (next to the CH2-bearing carbon), a plain methyl stub on C7, and NH in the five-membered ring. The benzene ring has, taking the piperidine-bearing carbon as 1: O-CH2-CH2-NHAc at position 2 (ortho) and HO2C at position 4 (para).
ref.notes: Typeset. Aromatic rings drawn with Kekule double bonds: benzene 3, indole 4. Methyl on the indole is an unlabeled stub.

wrong.substituent_description: A piperidine ring has EtO on C4 (solid wedge) and, on C2 next to N, a hashed bond to a circled benzene ring. That benzene ring carries, relative to the piperidine attachment at C1, an O-CH2CH2CH2-NHAc chain at C2 (ortho) and HO2C at C4 (para). The piperidine N is bonded through a CH2 to C4 of an indole (circled benzo ring) bearing MeO at C5 and an unlabelled methyl at C7, with NH in the five-membered ring and a drawn C2=C3 double bond.
wrong.notes: Handwritten drawing in black pen on white paper. Benzene rings drawn with circles; the only Kekule-style double bond is the indole five-membered ring C=C.

correct.substituent_description: A piperidine has EtO on a solid wedge at C4, a hashed bond from C2 (next to the ring N) to C1 of a circled benzene, and the ring N bonded to CH2 that is attached to an indole benzo ring. The benzene has O-CH2-CH2-NHAc at C2 (ortho to the piperidine attachment) and HO2C at C4 (para to the piperidine attachment). On the indole (circled benzo ring fused to a five-membered ring with NH and one drawn C=C), the CH2 link is at C4 (next to the fusion carbon C3a), MeO is at C5, and C7 (next to the NH-bearing fusion carbon) carries an unlabelled plain-line methyl stub.
correct.notes: Handwritten black ink on white paper. The ring N label has small stray tick marks. Two benzene rings are drawn as circles (the substituted phenyl and the indole benzo ring); the five-membered ring of the indole has one inner double line.

ref.substituent_description: A benzene ring (aromatic circle) bears C(=O)OEt on one carbon and, para to it, a CH=C(unlabeled methyl line)- double-bonded vinyl linker leading to a second aromatic-circle benzene ring. That second ring is fused to a saturated six-membered ring carrying two pairs of unlabeled line stubs (gem-dimethyl groups) on the two carbons flanking the ring; the vinyl linker is attached to the aromatic carbon adjacent to a ring-fusion carbon.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Carbonyl carbon is drawn as a loop/curl rather than a clean vertex
Unlabeled line ends (methyl groups) with small hook/arrow-like ticks at the ends of some
Exact attachment position of the vinyl linker on the fused aromatic ring is hard to judge
ref.notes: Handwritten, black ink, rough. Double bonds: 1 C=O and 1 C=C (alkene).

wrong.substituent_description: A piperidine has EtO on C4 via a solid wedge and, on C2 (adjacent to N), a benzene ring attached through a hashed bond. That benzene ring (circle) has, relative to the piperidine-bearing carbon C1: an O-CH2CH2CH2-NHAc chain at C2 (ortho) and HO2C at C4 (para to C1, meta to the O). The piperidine N is attached through a CH2 to C4 of an indole (benzene ring with circle; pyrrole ring with one drawn C=C and an NH), where the indole ring carries MeO on C5 (next to the CH2-bearing carbon) and an unlabelled methyl line on C7 (next to the NH-bearing ring fusion carbon).
overlaps_or_ambiguities: number of CH2 groups in the O-chain read as three from hand-drawn zigzag
methyl on indole is an unlabelled line end
wrong.notes: Handwritten. Aromatic rings: both benzene rings have circles; the five-membered ring has one drawn double bond.

correct.substituent_description: A piperidine (6-ring with N) has EtO on a solid wedge on C4 (counting N as 1 and going through the carbon next to the aryl-bearing carbon: N1, C2 bears aryl on a hashed bond, C3 CH2, C4 bears EtO), and the ring N is attached through a CH2 to C4 of an indole. The aryl on piperidine C2 is a benzene (circle) bearing, relative to the piperidine attachment at C1, an O-CH2-CH2-NHAc chain at C2 (ortho) and HO2C at C4 (para). The indole (benzene circle fused to a pyrrole ring with NH and a C=C double bond) has the CH2N at C4, MeO at C5 (adjacent to C4) and an unlabeled methyl line at C7.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Methyl at the right of the indole is only a short unlabeled line
Stray tick mark beside the piperidine N label
Indole is drawn with a circle in the six-ring but a Kekule C=C in the five-ring
correct.notes: Handwritten, black ink on white. One double bond (indole C2=C3). One solid wedge (EtO) and one hashed bond (to the aryl). No written stereo descriptors.
